chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Nazarro's standing ovation at the Boston Conservatory
summary: At the Night of the Great Renowns the emcee introduces Nazarro, who bows and walks off, teaching the boys showmanship.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Can you tell me that story about Nat Nazarra coming out on stage?

Oh, yes. That was at the Boston Conservatory of Music they used to have a show was called the Night of the Great Renowns, and this particular night Nazarra had been having Buck and Bubbles and Chuck and Chuckles off and on at the Boston Conservatory of Music. But one particular night there the master of ceremonies knew who Mr. Nat Nazarra was, and he -- he hadn't introduced him, and it sounded like some kind of honor like, see. So he says that, you know, we've been having featured acts here in the Boston Conservatory of Music for quite -- many years now, and we owe our thanks to a manager who manages some of the acts, especially Buck and Bubles and an act you're going to see tonight, Chuck and Chuckles, and he said, now,

ladies and gentlemen, let's welcome the manager of Buck and Bubbles and Chuck and Chuckles, Nat Nazarro.1) And the audience stood up. He got a standing ovation, and he was a very proud man, Nat Nazarra. He walked out on the stage, walked to the center of the stage and bowed, thanked the audience, you know, and he didn't say a word. And he stopped the show. He walked off the other side of the stage.

Then the master of ceremonies come back onstage, and he had to actually beg the audience to let them continue the show. And then sometime later in the dressing room backstage Mr. Nazarra, he come up to Chuckles and I, he say, "You see that, cats?" He says, "That's how to do it, you see. That's what you call showmanship."
So we were very proud of him, you know. He was a wonderful man. We're going to miss him very much -- and --
